name: Apollos
charge: Being instructed in the way of the Lord, and receiving correction from a tentmaker and his wife
summary: A certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man and mighty in the scriptures, came to Ephesus; he was instructed in the way of the Lord and being fervent in the spirit he spoke and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John. Aquila and Priscilla heard him speak boldly in the synagogue, took him to themselves, and expounded the way of God more perfectly. He then passed into Achaia and helped them much which had believed. Paul afterward refused to be set against him, saying he had planted and Apollos watered, but God gave the increase.
offenseFull: A certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man and mighty in the scriptures, came to Ephesus (Acts 18:24). Note where he was born. We always had settlements in Egypt, which is why the angel told Joseph to take the young child and his mother and flee into Egypt rather than into a strange people (Matthew 2:13); a man of our nation born and raised at Alexandria is another witness of that settlement, and he came out of it mighty in the scriptures. Eloquent means articulate, well spoken, a man who can hold a room with his speech; and mighty in the scriptures means he knew the law.

He was instructed in the way of the Lord, and being fervent in the spirit he spoke and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John; and when Aquila and Priscilla had heard him speak boldly in the synagogue they took him to themselves and expounded the way of God to him more perfectly (Acts 18:25-26). Fervent means he had a passionate intensity about it, and bold means he did not care what it cost him to say what the Lord said; some brothers cannot even confront their own household, and this one stood up in a synagogue. John’s teaching had spread and men were carrying it and talking it among themselves, so what he held was real as far as it went;

the water baptism he knew was the whole of what he knew. That is the same condition Paul had been in, a man taught the law by the best teacher in Israel who had not yet been shown that the law was speaking of Christ. What was missing was supplied by a tentmaker and his wife without a public contest. He did not refuse it, and the diligence he already had was joined to the fuller word.
judgmentFull: When he was disposed to pass into Achaia, the brethren wrote exhorting the disciples to receive him, and when he was come he helped them much which had believed through grace, for he mightily convinced the Jews, and that publicly, showing by the scriptures that Jesus was Christ (Acts 18:27-28). His strength was in what he could establish out of the writings, not in eloquence by itself.

At Corinth the people took his name and made a party out of it, every one saying, I am of Paul, and I of Apollos, and I of Cephas, and I of Christ (1 Corinthians 1:12). Paul refused the comparison and answered it with the order of the work: who then is Paul, and who is Apollos, but ministers by whom they believed; he had planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase, so neither is he that planteth any thing, neither he that watereth, and every man shall receive his own reward according to his own labour (1 Corinthians 3:5-8). That is the same order seen at Samaria, where Philip the deacon planted and the apostles came and watered (Acts 8:14-17). Paul kept him as a brother and afterward greatly desired him to come to Corinth with the brethren, though his will was not at all to come at that time (1 Corinthians 16:12).

Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

text.text: And a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, and mighty in the scriptures, came to Ephesus.

And when they were departed, behold, the angel of the Lord appeareth to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I bring thee word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.
This man was instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in the spirit, he spake and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John.
And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue: whom when Aquila and Priscilla had heard, they took him unto them, and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.
And when he was disposed to pass into Achaia, the brethren wrote, exhorting the disciples to receive him: who, when he was come, helped them much which had believed through grace:
For he mightily convinced the Jews, and that publickly, shewing by the scriptures that Jesus was Christ.
Now this I say, that every one of you saith, I am of Paul; and I of Apollos; and I of Cephas; and I of Christ.
Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos, but ministers by whom ye believed, even as the Lord gave to every man?
I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase.
So then neither is he that planteth any thing, neither he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase.
Now he that planteth and he that watereth are one: and every man shall receive his own reward according to his own labour.
Now when the apostles which were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John:
Who, when they were come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Ghost:
(For as yet he was fallen upon none of them: only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.)
Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.
As touching our brother Apollos, I greatly desired him to come unto you with the brethren: but his will was not at all to come at this time; but he will come when he shall have convenient time.
Bring Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey diligently, that nothing be wanting unto them.
